messages:
ben_customer: Hey team — we started seeing streaming responses drop early for a production customer. They get a few SSE events, then the connection is closed by the server and the client reconnects. Happens behind their corporate proxy (nginx) but also repros locally if we slow the client reader. Partial chunks show up in our logs. Billing spiked because the client reconnects every 10s and each reconnect counts as new request. Not sure if it's our runtime aborting due to backpressure or the proxy timing out. Stack excerpt:

ben_customer: server logs show: `write() failed: Broken pipe` and `write returned EAGAIN` alternating, then `connection aborted after 12000ms write-timeout`.

alice_support: thanks for the report — can you paste a minimal repro and the exact headers the client uses? also which runtime version is this on?

ben_customer: runtime: rwinf-runtime v2.2.8 (hosted). Repro script (node) — slow reader that intentionally sleeps 1s per chunk: 
```
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
async function slowRead() {
 const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=...',{ headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer X' }});
 const reader = res.body.getReader();
 while(true){
   const {done, value} = await reader.read();
   if(done) break;
   await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,1000)); // slow consumer
   process.stdout.write(new TextDecoder().decode(value));
 }
}
slowRead();
```
This reliably reproduces within ~10s.

cassandra_oncall: adding logs from our edge: 
```
[edge] 2026-11-12T18:21:33Z conn=xyz write err: EAGAIN after 16k bytes
[edge] 2026-11-12T18:21:33Z conn=xyz retrying write, pending_bytes=475912
[edge] 2026-11-12T18:21:33Z conn=xyz aborting connection: write stalled > write_timeout
```
Also seeing `proxy_buffering on`for customer's nginx config via their ops screenshot.

alice_support: ok, two things to check: (1) proxy/nginx buffering and http version / chunked handshake, (2) runtime-level max pending bytes and write timeouts. If nginx has `proxy_buffering on` it will attempt to buffer the entire response — with a slow consumer that triggers memory/backpressure and can lead to upstream aborts. Ask customer to try `proxy_buffering off` and `proxy_http_version 1.1` with `chunked_transfer_encoding on` for SSE.

ben_customer: tried toggling `proxy_buffering off` and set `proxy_http_version 1.1` — saw improvement (longer stream) but still hit aborts around ~30s in heavy throughput cases. Also they use an HTTP/2 frontend for other endpoints; SSE should use HTTP/1.1 ideally.

dan_eng_runtime: thanks for the details — the runtime v2.2.8 has a conservative backpressure abort: we cap per-connection pending bytes to 256k and a write stall timeout of 10s. If the consumer keeps the TCP read window closed we escalate and abort to avoid head-of-line blocking of the GPU worker queue. Two notes:
- If you can, set a higher per-connection limit (temporary) via `sse.max_pending_bytes` and increase `sse.write_timeout_ms`.
- Long-term fix: we shipped a backpressure mitigation in v2.3.1 that does adaptive batching + incremental writes to avoid EAGAIN thrash with slow consumers and proxies that hold the window.

alice_support: dan, can you paste the recommended config knobs and a safe rollout path? customer is on hosted (can't edit all knobs) — any hosted-side quick fixes we can flip?

dan_eng_runtime: suggested knobs (strings below for their ops):
```
# server-side tunables (name:value)
sse.max_pending_bytes: 524288
sse.write_timeout_ms: 30000
sse.incremental_write_size: 4096
```
For hosted customers we can enable a per-tenant override. I'll propose a temporary increase for the tenant until they migrate to runtime v2.3.1. Also recommend the consumer implement exponential reconnect with Last-Event-ID to avoid billing storms on flappy connections.

ben_customer: that sounds good. Also — how about client-side best practice to avoid server aborts? They are a javascript single-threaded client reading chunks slowly during heavy UI work.

cassandra_oncall: client tips: read the stream on a worker/Background task (avoid UI main thread), drain fast enough (or apply flow control: pause/resume on the Fetch stream), and use backoff on reconnect. For Node/browser: buffer small chunks and flush to UI at intervals rather than block the stream read loop.

alice_support: replicated steps for hosted tenant: opened a ticket with eng-runtime to flip `sse.max_pending_bytes` for tenant id t-7g4. Also added a task to roll out runtime v2.3.1 to the affected infra pool. tagging @dan_eng_runtime for the change.

dan_eng_runtime: started a canary deploy of runtime v2.3.1 to the edge pool serving that tenant. Deploy-bot will post results.

deply-bot: (automated) sorry typo in bot name — replaced with actual entry below.

deply-bot would be a mistake — we'll use deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: eng-runtime v2.3.1 -> pool-us-west-2-canary. status: success. rollouts: 10% -> 50% -> 100% planned.

ben_customer: after the canary we still saw one reconnect but payloads are no longer truncated and no EAGAIN churn in the logs. Billing spike subsided after we applied jitter + backoff in the client.

alice_support: rolled the per-tenant override (sse.max_pending_bytes=524288, sse.write_timeout_ms=30000) for t-7g4. Please monitor for any memory spikes and report.

ben_customer: confirmed. No more abrupt server aborts in 48h. client implemented Last-Event-ID reconnect and exponential backoff — billing returned to baseline. thanks :tada:

alice_support: summary + action items:
- root cause: slow consumer (corporate proxy + client main-thread) causing TCP write window stall -> EAGAIN -> runtime aborts to protect worker queue
- mitigations applied: nginx proxy_buffering off recommended, tenant-level `sse.max_pending_bytes` increased, runtime v2.3.1 rolled out with adaptive incremental writes
- customer actions: move stream read off UI thread, implement reconnect backoff + Last-Event-ID, consider using dedicated capacity if they need guaranteed throughput
- follow-up: eng-runtime to watch metrics for memory and per-conn pending bytes for 7 days (assigned to @dan_eng_runtime)

cassandra_oncall: noted — closing oncall loop, if anything flares re-open.

ben_customer: closing from customer side as well. thanks everyone :) :thumbsup:
